line_fields.name: ancestor_ids
line_fields.means: the identities of the blocks of ancestors, item by item, as block records give them in identity

line_fields.name: ancestors
line_fields.means: the types of the blocks that hold the leaf block of the line, innermost first; empty for a line of no leaf block

line_fields.name: attached_here
line_fields.means: a block whose attribute block the parse attached starts on this line

line_fields.name: blank
line_fields.means: the line is no line of a leaf block and holds nothing but spaces and tabs after the prefixes of its containers, so a bare quote mark is a blank line of its quote and `>>` at column 1 is text

line_fields.name: body
line_fields.means: the line from body_start to its end, without trailing spaces and tabs

line_fields.name: body_end
line_fields.means: the end of body

line_fields.name: body_start
line_fields.means: where the text of the line starts behind its container prefixes and indent: on a line of a leaf block, where the parse puts the leaf's text on that line, the marker of an item, description or footnote body on its marker line and the quote marks of the open quotes being prefixes up to their content column; on a lazy line, which carries no prefix of the containers it does not reach, its first character that is not a space or tab; on a line of a leaf of `verbatim_leaves` whose prefixes the parse does not place, behind its leading spaces and tabs and as many quote marks followed by a space as quotes hold the leaf, since a further mark is content; on any other line, behind its leading spaces and tabs and its quote marks that are followed by a space or end the line

line_fields.name: closes_container
line_fields.means: the line is a bare colon run that closes an open colon container

line_fields.name: end
line_fields.means: the end of the line before its terminator

line_fields.name: lazy
line_fields.means: a later line of a text leaf that carries fewer quote marks than the quotes that hold the leaf, or whose body starts left of the content column of the innermost item, description or footnote body that holds it: a line that no open container owns and that continues the paragraph

line_fields.name: leaf
line_fields.means: the type of the innermost leaf block that holds the line (a text leaf, a verbatim leaf or table_row), or none

line_fields.name: leaf_first
line_fields.means: the line is the first line of its leaf block

line_fields.name: leaf_head
line_fields.means: the first line of the leaf block of the line; absent for a line of no leaf block

line_fields.name: leaf_id
line_fields.means: an identity of the leaf block of the line, equal on two lines exactly when one leaf block holds both

line_fields.name: leaf_next
line_fields.means: the line below the last line of the leaf block of the line, or the line below for a line of no leaf block; absent at the end of the document

line_fields.name: leaf_start
line_fields.means: where the leaf block of the line starts in the source; absent for a line of no leaf block

line_fields.name: next
line_fields.means: the line below, absent on the last line; next2 is the second line below

line_fields.name: number
line_fields.means: the line number, from 1

line_fields.name: open_colon
line_fields.means: the colon containers open where the line starts, innermost first: each a div of any name (a directive, an admonition and a figure group included), a line block or a hard-break block, with width (the length of its opener run), line and column (1-based, of the opener) and kind (div, admonition, figure group, line block or hard-break block); only those opened inside the innermost quote, list item, footnote or description that holds the line, since a run cannot close a container outside its owner (C2-B-109)

line_fields.name: prev
line_fields.means: the line above, absent on line 1; prev2 is the second line above

line_fields.name: quote_depth
line_fields.means: the number of quotes that hold the leaf of the line

line_fields.name: quote_marks
line_fields.means: the number of quote marks at the start of the line, each after optional spaces and tabs and followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line

line_fields.name: quote_prefix
line_fields.means: the line before body_start holds a quote mark, so the line carries a prefix of a quote

line_fields.name: raw_body
line_fields.means: body as written in the source, without the U+0000 that text and body read for hidden characters

line_fields.name: shape
line_fields.means: the name of the line shape of line-shapes.json that body has, read without the requires and at conditions of a shape, so a closer, frontmatter and a continuation row are not told apart from the shapes they share a first character with; text when no other shape matches, blank for an empty body

line_fields.name: start
line_fields.means: the first character of the line

line_fields.name: text
line_fields.means: the whole line without its terminator, each character of an autolink, a code, math, raw or literal span, an inline comment, an include, a link reference or abbreviation definition, and each escaped punctuation character with its backslash, read as U+0000

block_fields.name: after_quote_mark
block_fields.means: the text before opener_start on its line ends with a quote mark and its space

block_fields.name: ancestor_ids
block_fields.means: the identities of the blocks that hold the block, innermost first, the document last; the identity of a block is equal on two records exactly when they stand for one node

block_fields.name: ancestors
block_fields.means: the types of the blocks that hold the block, innermost first, the document last

block_fields.name: attributed
block_fields.means: the block has an attached attribute block, so its source starts at the attribute line

block_fields.name: column
block_fields.means: the column of start, counted after the quote marks of the quotes that hold the block, with tab stops

block_fields.name: end
block_fields.means: the end of the block in the source

block_fields.name: identity
block_fields.means: the identity of the block, equal to the entry that ancestor_ids gives for it in the records of the blocks it holds

block_fields.name: image_line
block_fields.means: the block is a paragraph that holds a single image, a block image line

block_fields.name: index
block_fields.means: the position of the block among the blocks of its owner, from 0

block_fields.name: item_owner
block_fields.means: the list item that is owner, or that holds owner through colon containers only (a div, admonition, directive or figure group); the document when there is none. Its content_column and marker_column are those of owner

block_fields.name: last_line
block_fields.means: the line record of the last line of the block

block_fields.name: layout
block_fields.means: the entry of the block in the source layout, whose facts are read by name with a dotted path (layout.markerColumn); a fact the entry does not have, or a block with no entry, is absent

block_fields.name: line
block_fields.means: the first line of the block

block_fields.name: mark_column
block_fields.means: the column of opener_start, counted as column is

block_fields.name: node
block_fields.means: the node of the tree that the record stands for, whose fields are those of the AST document and are read by name with a dotted path; a field the node does not have is absent

block_fields.name: opener_column
block_fields.means: the marker column of the block where it has a marker and no attached attribute block, otherwise column

block_fields.name: opener_start
block_fields.means: where the opening mark of the block starts: start, or for an attributed block the first character after its attribute lines and any comment-only lines between them and the block, the spaces, tabs and the quote marks of the quotes that hold the block before it skipped

block_fields.name: opener_text
block_fields.means: the line from opener_start to its end, without trailing spaces and tabs

block_fields.name: owner
block_fields.means: the block that holds this one, a description list skipped; the document when there is none. Its content_column is 0 for the document and a quote, the content column of an item, description or footnote body, and the column of its first line for any other owner; its marker_column is the marker column of an item

block_fields.name: parent
block_fields.means: the block that directly holds this one, with the same content_column and marker_column as owner has

block_fields.name: prev_type
block_fields.means: the type of the block directly before this one among the blocks of its parent; absent for the first

block_fields.name: start
block_fields.means: the first character of the block's source

block_fields.name: text
block_fields.means: the source of the block from start to end

block_fields.name: type
block_fields.means: the node type of the block

inline_fields.name: end
inline_fields.means: the end of the node in the source

inline_fields.name: key_text
inline_fields.means: for a link reference, the plain text of its stored key read as inline content as C2-I-084 requires; absent otherwise

inline_fields.name: leaf
inline_fields.means: the type of the leaf block whose inline content holds the node

inline_fields.name: node
inline_fields.means: the node of the tree that the record stands for, whose fields are those of the AST document and are read by name with a dotted path; a field the node does not have is absent, and a text run has no node

inline_fields.name: parent
inline_fields.means: the type of the node that holds the node, the leaf block for a node at the top of the content

inline_fields.name: raw_ref
inline_fields.means: for a link or an image with a key: its reference from the opening bracket to the bracket that closes its label, the image mark left out, read without the container prefixes of the lines it crosses; otherwise its text

inline_fields.name: start
inline_fields.means: the start of the node in the source

inline_fields.name: text
inline_fields.means: the source of the node from start to end

inline_fields.name: type
inline_fields.means: the node type, or `text_run` for a text run (C2-W-140)

attribute_fields.name: end
attribute_fields.means: the end of the part: behind its name, behind the closing quote of a quoted value, or behind an unquoted value

attribute_fields.name: entries
attribute_fields.means: for a key: the number of comma-separated entries of its value, one more than its commas; 0 for an id, a class or a language

attribute_fields.name: entry_total
attribute_fields.means: for a key: the exact sum of its comma-separated entries, spaces around an entry ignored, each read as a decimal number; 0 when an entry is no decimal number, and for an id, a class or a language

attribute_fields.name: index
attribute_fields.means: the place of the part among the attribute parts of its owner in source order, from 0

attribute_fields.name: kept
attribute_fields.means: the part is a key that the owner keeps in its `attrs` in the tree, so that no construct consumed it (C2-B-227)

attribute_fields.name: key
attribute_fields.means: for a key: its name as written; empty for an id, a class or a language

attribute_fields.name: key_end
attribute_fields.means: the end of the name of a key; for an id, a class or a language, the end of the part

attribute_fields.name: kind
attribute_fields.means: `id`, `class`, `lang` or `key`: which part of C2-I-029 this is

attribute_fields.name: last_key
attribute_fields.means: the part is a key and no later part of the same owner has that name, so its value is the one the owner keeps

attribute_fields.name: owner
attribute_fields.means: the node that the attribute block attaches to, with the fields of `attribute_owner_fields`

attribute_fields.name: semantic
attribute_fields.means: the part is a key whose name, in the letter case written, is a semantic span key: `abbr`, `time`, `kbd` or one a registered extension adds

attribute_fields.name: semantic_value
attribute_fields.means: the part is a semantic span key whose value the element carries (`abbr` as title, `time` as datetime)

attribute_fields.name: start
attribute_fields.means: where the part starts in the source: its `#`, `.` or `:`, or the first character of its key

attribute_fields.name: text
attribute_fields.means: the part as written, from start to end

attribute_fields.name: value
attribute_fields.means: the id, class or language name, or the value of a key with its quotes removed and its escapes read; empty for a bare key

attribute_owner_fields.name: align_overlap
attribute_owner_fields.means: for a table: the numbers of the columns, from 1 and joined by single spaces, where the column takes a horizontal alignment from `aligns` and the cell of the first head row carries a horizontal alignment mark

attribute_owner_fields.name: body_rows
attribute_owner_fields.means: for a table: the number of rows of its body groups

attribute_owner_fields.name: columns
attribute_owner_fields.means: for a table: its number of columns, the cell count of its widest row

attribute_owner_fields.name: foot_rows
attribute_owner_fields.means: for a table: the number of rows of its foot

attribute_owner_fields.name: format
attribute_owner_fields.means: for a table: `pipe` for a pipe table, `csv` or `tsv` for a delimited table; empty otherwise

attribute_owner_fields.name: head_rows
attribute_owner_fields.means: for a table: the number of rows of its head

attribute_owner_fields.name: node
attribute_owner_fields.means: the node of the tree, read as the `node` of a block or inline record (C2-W-140)

attribute_owner_fields.name: opener_start
attribute_owner_fields.means: for a block: where its own text starts behind its attribute lines and any comment-only lines between them and the block, behind the indent and the quote marks of the quotes that hold it; for an item, a cell or an inline node, its start

attribute_owner_fields.name: start
attribute_owner_fields.means: the start of the node, which for a block that took attribute lines is the first of them

attribute_owner_fields.name: type
attribute_owner_fields.means: the node type of the owner

attribute_owner_fields.name: valign_overlap
attribute_owner_fields.means: for a table: the numbers of the columns, as `align_overlap` writes them, where the column takes a vertical alignment from `valigns`, the cell of the first head row carries a vertical alignment mark, and the column is not in `align_overlap`

id_fields.name: heading_text
id_fields.means: for a heading id, the plain text of that heading read as C2-I-084 reads it; absent for every other id

id_fields.name: id
id_fields.means: an id carried by the tree or an id or name in the rendered HTML, including authored ids, generated heading ids, footnote or note mark ids, and raw HTML anchors

id_fields.name: index
id_fields.means: the position of the record among the id records, counted from 0

id_fields.name: owner
id_fields.means: the type of the first node in document order that carries the id, the one it anchors

id_fields.name: rendered
id_fields.means: some occurrence of this id or name is present in the rendered HTML under the options of the run

id_fields.name: start
id_fields.means: the start in the source of the first node that carries the id, 0 when that node has no position

id_fields.name: xref
id_fields.means: the id is a cross-reference target: a heading or a numbered caption owner, including a table, figure, figure group or numbered panel

table_fields.name: group
table_fields.means: on a table_row or table_cell record: the type of the group that holds the row, `table_head`, `table_body` or `table_foot`

table_fields.name: row_index
table_fields.means: on a table_row or table_cell record: the position of the row among the rows of its group, from 0

table_fields.name: source_format
table_fields.means: on a table, table_row or table_cell record: the source format of the table, `pipe` for a pipe table, `csv` or `tsv` for a delimited table; spelling that the tree does not hold

table_fields.name: table_above
table_fields.means: on a line record of a line in the source of a pipe table, from its first line to its last: the nearest line above it in that source whose raw_body does not start with `%%`; absent where there is none and outside a pipe table

table_fields.name: table_below
table_fields.means: as table_above, the nearest such line below it

block.names: the node of the block record

inline.names: the node of the inline record

text_run.names: the node whose children make the run, the node with inline content that holds it; never a text or soft break child

attribute.names: the owner of the attribute record

line.names: the leaf block of the line: the block with inline content that holds it (a paragraph, a heading, a term, a line of a line block, a cell paragraph, the paragraph of a caption), a verbatim leaf, or the table_row of a line of a pipe table; for a line of no leaf block the innermost block whose source holds the line, and the document where none does
